name: Friedrich Mayer

events.title: Acknowledged paternity of son Friedrich
events.description: Son Friedrich born 11 Jan 1862 to the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier. Before the parish priest and witnesses, the single mason Friedrich Mayer, legitimate son of the citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and Juliana Senn, declared himself the father and asked that the child bear his surname with full rights. Godparents: Joseph Wenz, shoemaker (his brother-in-law), and Sophie Mayer, of age, single, in service at Freiburg, daughter of Heinrich Mayer.

bioAdditions:
The Munzingen birth register for 1862 explains why Friedrich and Maria Anna married in October 1862. Their first child, Friedrich, was born on 11 Jan 1862 at 9:30 a.m. and baptized on 13 January as the illegitimate son of 'the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier', daughter of the late master joiner Servatius Birkenmaier and Agatha Heitzler. In the same entry the single mason Friedrich Mayer, son of the citizen and master mason Heinrich Mayer and Juliana Senn, freely declared himself the father before the priest and the witnesses. He asked that the child carry his surname and have all the rights of an acknowledged child. The godparents were family: Joseph Wenz, shoemaker of Munzingen and husband of Friedrich's sister Maria Anna Creszentia, and Friedrich's unmarried sister Sophie Mayer, then in domestic service at Freiburg (S1). The parents married nine months later, on 20 Oct 1862. This birth date, 11 Jan 1862, matches the date the son himself gave on his 1886 Luzerne marriage docket ('11 January 1862', Hazleton) (S2), and it corrects the tree's 11 Nov 1862.

In America the family's spelling kept shifting. Friedrich's eldest son appears as 'Fred Meir' in 1886 (S2), and probably as 'Fred Meires' of Hazleton in the 1915 state death index (see Frederick Meier). Friedrich's own son Henry J. died in Wilkes-Barre on 20 Dec 1950, not in 1940 (see Henry J. Meier).
funFacts: His first son was born nine months before the wedding. Friedrich went to the priest two days after the birth to acknowledge the boy as his own, and his sister and brother-in-law stood as godparents.

openQuestionsNew: Emigration still not found. The Munzingen 1862 birth and marriage entries carry no emigration note in what was read. The Auswanderungsakten of Bezirksamt Freiburg (Staatsarchiv Freiburg) for 1867–68 remain the best lead.
